pages.name: Quick Reference
pages.html:
Everything the Lantern gives Sylas, he pays for, usually in hit points, Hit Dice or something he will regret knowing. It is the only item in the set that refills at dusk.

Wondrous item, legacy item (requires attunement by Sylas)

Your Charges

The Vigil Charges pool grows on its own at 6th, 10th and 15th level. You never have to update the sheet — the number just changes.

StateYour levelVigil ChargesBack at dusk
Dormantlevels 3–53all of them
Awakenedlevels 6–95all of them
Exaltedlevels 10–1471d6 + 1
Legendarylevel 15+91d8 + 1

At Dormant and Awakened every spent charge comes back. From 10th level it stops refilling completely: the pool is bigger, and a heavy day stays expensive into the next one.

Legacy Save DC

Where a feature makes something roll a saving throw, the DC is 8 + proficiency bonus + spellcasting ability modifier. It comes off your sheet, so it rises as you do.

What Unlocks When

Features arrive on their own. Below its level a feature is not on the item at all, so anything you can see on the sheet is something you can use. Where a later state improves an earlier feature, the old version disappears and the new one takes its place.

Dormant — levels 3–5 (Uncommon): Mortuary Light; Shepherd's Questions; Knowledge Has a Price.

Awakened — levels 6–9 (Rare): Ask the Dead; Hold the Door; Forbidden Inquiry.

Exalted — levels 10–14 (Very Rare): Take Their Burden; The Soul Waits; Autopsy of the Impossible.

Legendary — level 15+ (Legendary): Shepherd Between Worlds; Not Yet; Let Me Understand.

The Part That Is Not Automatic

Not Yet has no automatic recharge at all, because it does not come back on a rest. Once it is spent it stays spent until your DM clears it.

Advancing

Reaching the level makes the next state possible. What actually wakes the item is the moment named at the top of each state below — a choice, not an achievement, and never something you can win in a fight. You do not need to chase it. When it happens, you will know, and so will the item.

pages.name: Levels 3–5 — Dormant
pages.html:
Uncommon · levels 3–5 · 3 Vigil Charges, all of them restored at dusk

Where it starts. This is the item as you first receive it. Everything below is yours from the moment you attune.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

Mortuary Light

1 minute — no cost

By touching a corpse for 1 minute, Sylas learns its approximate time of death, whether death primarily resulted from violence, disease, poison, magic or natural causes, and whether necromancy affected it after death.

Shepherd's Questions

No action — 1 charge

Sylas can expend 1 charge to gain advantage on one Arcana, Investigation, Medicine, Nature or Religion check concerning a corpse, an undead creature, a curse, a planar phenomenon, a supernatural disease or a ritual.

Knowledge Has a Price

No action — 1d6 necrotic per proficiency bonus

After failing such a check, Sylas can take 1d6 necrotic damage per proficiency bonus to reroll it. This damage cannot be reduced or prevented. Once used, this feature cannot be used again until he finishes a short or long rest.

pages.name: Levels 6–9 — Awakened
pages.html:
Rare · levels 6–9 · 5 Vigil Charges, all of them restored at dusk

What wakes it. Sylas knowingly accepts a meaningful personal consequence in exchange for knowledge capable of protecting another person.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

Ask the Dead

Action — 3 charges — 10 minutes

Sylas can expend 3 charges to cast speak with dead.

Hold the Door

Hold the Door. Reaction — 2 charges

Hold the Door — The Price. No action — 2d8 necrotic

When a creature within 30 feet would drop to 0 hit points, Sylas can use his reaction and expend 2 charges. It instead drops to 1. Sylas takes 2d8 necrotic damage that cannot be reduced or prevented.

Forbidden Inquiry

1 minute — 1 Hit Die · 1× per long rest

Once per long rest, Sylas can spend one Hit Die while examining a creature, corpse, object or supernatural phenomenon for 1 minute. He may ask the DM one factual question concerning its nature, origin, condition, vulnerabilities or magical properties. The answer must be truthful but need not reveal information that no available divinatory magic could reasonably determine. The Hit Die remains spent normally.

pages.name: Levels 10–14 — Exalted
pages.html:
Very Rare · levels 10–14 · 7 Vigil Charges, regaining 1d6 + 1 at dusk

What wakes it. Sylas encounters something that fundamentally challenges his understanding of death or cosmic order and chooses understanding over denial without surrendering his principles.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

Take Their Burden

Action — 3 charges

As an action, Sylas can touch a willing creature and expend 3 charges to transfer one of the following from it to himself: blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, poisoned, one disease, or one curse affecting only that creature. The original target is freed. Sylas receives the condition, disease or curse for its remaining duration and receives no saving throw against the initial transfer. If the effect requires ongoing saves, Sylas makes them normally.

The Soul Waits

Reaction — 3 charges — 1 minute

When a creature dies within 30 feet, Sylas can use his reaction and expend 3 charges. For 1 minute its soul cannot be unwillingly transformed, trapped or consumed, its corpse cannot become undead, and resurrection magic cast upon it requires no material component worth 300 gp or less. This does not resurrect the creature.

Autopsy of the Impossible

1 minute — 2 charges

After observing a creature for 1 minute, Sylas may expend 2 charges to learn two of the following:

  • damage immunities;
  • damage resistances;
  • damage vulnerabilities;
  • condition immunities;
  • highest saving throw;
  • lowest saving throw;
  • whether it has Legendary Resistance;
  • creature type;
  • one special trait chosen by the DM that materially defines the creature.

A creature cannot be examined this way again until Sylas finishes a long rest.

pages.name: Level 15+ — Legendary
pages.html:
Legendary · level 15+ · 9 Vigil Charges, regaining 1d8 + 1 at dusk

What wakes it. Sylas is given the opportunity to violate the natural boundary of death for something he desperately wants, and consciously defines where his line lies.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

Shepherd Between Worlds

Passive. Always on. Nothing to click and nothing to spend.

Sylas constantly sees 30 feet into the Ethereal Plane, and can perceive invisible undead within 30 feet even if he cannot otherwise see invisible creatures.

Not Yet

Reaction — 5 charges · once, then reset by hand — it does not return on a rest

When a creature within 60 feet dies, Sylas can use his reaction and expend 5 charges. Its body falls dead normally, but its soul remains beside him as a visible spectral presence until the end of his next turn. Before then, Sylas may use an action to return the soul. The creature returns to life with 1 hit point, 2 levels of exhaustion, and no benefit from healing until the end of its next turn. Once Sylas successfully restores a creature this way, he cannot use Not Yet again until 7 days have passed. This cannot restore a creature that died of old age or whose soul is unwilling or unavailable.

Let Me Understand

1 minute — 3 Hit Dice · 1× per long rest

Once per long rest, Sylas can spend 3 Hit Dice and spend 1 minute studying a creature, artifact, corpse, curse or supernatural phenomenon. The DM must reveal three materially useful truths concerning it. At least one must concern a weakness, limitation, cost, method of destruction, method of cure or means by which it can be opposed, if such information exists. Sylas' ultimate weapon is not death. It is knowing what everyone else was afraid to examine.

pages.name: Playing It Well
pages.html:
Everything the Lantern gives Sylas, he pays for, usually in hit points, Hit Dice or something he will regret knowing. It is the only item in the set that refills at dusk.

At the Table

  • Charges return at dusk, not dawn. A night's long rest refills nothing. His day starts full and empties as it goes, so the hard question is always whether tonight is the night.
  • Knowledge Has a Price gets worse as he gets better. It is 1d6 per proficiency bonus and it cannot be reduced or prevented — no resistance, no absorption, no temporary hit points spared.
  • Hold the Door is the best two charges on the item and the most dangerous. Read his own hit points before offering, because the 2d8 cannot be mitigated either.
  • Hit Dice spent on knowledge stay spent. Forbidden Inquiry and Let Me Understand cost him hit points he will not be able to recover that night.
  • Autopsy of the Impossible before a boss is worth more than anything he can cast. Highest and lowest saving throw tells the entire party what to aim.

Questions That Come Up

Does Not Yet come back on a rest?
No. Seven days, tracked by hand — the item deliberately has no automatic recovery on that one, so it cannot hand the use back early.

Can Take Their Burden move a condition he is immune to?
He takes it on for its remaining duration; if he is immune it ends at once. He still spends the charges, and the original target is still freed.

Can Hold the Door be used on himself?
He is a creature within 30 feet of himself, so yes — but he then takes 2d8 he cannot prevent, which may not leave him better off. Do the arithmetic first.

Does The Soul Waits bring anyone back?
No. It protects a soul and a body for a minute and makes somebody else's resurrection cheaper.

Does Mortuary Light cost a charge?
No. Touching a corpse for a minute is free, and it is the feature he should be using most often.

If Something Here Disagrees With the Item

The item on your sheet is the rules. This journal is generated from the same source, so the two should never differ — but if they do, the item wins and your DM should know.
